question_text: Explain an algorithm that restores stock for a selected product using the lastn entries of a chronological singly linked sales log. Each node stores product, quantity and next; head is the old est. Add quantities only for the selected product; count n across all recent entries, leave the log unchanged, and report invalidn.
adaptation_rationale: Original application rewritten to be self-contained; assessed reasoning retained within cited 2027 scope.
solution: Count total entries without changing links.; Reject n<0 orn greater than the log length with appropriate error handling.; Start at head and skip length-n nodes.; Traverse the remaining n recent entries.; For entries whose product is the selected product, add that quantity to its stock.; Do not alter nodes/next links or restore entries outside then-entry window.
